transcript: Teal's resume builder gives you multiple ways to turn weak, vague bullets into strong, metrics-driven ones. Here, I have three bullets that need work. I'll start with managed a team. Clicking improve with AI reveals five modes. Automatic generates a bullet instantly. Keywords pulls relevant terms from your matched job description. Job description draws in the actual roles and responsibilities from that job. Coach me walks you through building a strong bullet step-by-step. Custom prompt lets you give the AI a specific direction, like make it concise or focus on teamwork. I'll go with automatic. This option aligns best with what I was going for. I'll select it and click save. The bullet updates on the resume immediately. You can also improve a bullet directly inside the text editor. Hit improve with AI for the same five modes. Or choose write with AI to generate a new bullet from scratch. Teal uses your experience and context to produce options you can edit from there. I'll select this one and fill in the placeholder. Developed a multi-channel communication strategy that improved customer engagement by 25% in 3 months. Click save. If you start typing a bullet and get stuck, like help to develop, click finish with AI and Teal will complete it based on where you were headed. And if you want different options after generating, just click regenerate. For this last bullet, I'll use the keywords mode to inform the new bullet. I'll select customer satisfaction as my target keyword. Teal shows me exactly where that keyword appears and generates options around it. I'll take this first bullet, fill in the metric, 37%, and save. And that bullet is ready to use on any resume in Teal. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
